A release of fixes and speed-ups since 1.0.0. Your configuration keeps
working as it is.

## What's new

- Opening the vault is quicker. You can type the master password while
  "Starting Bitwarden CLI…" is still on screen, and `Enter` unlocks as soon
  as `bw` is ready. After the unlock the panes fill in within a quarter of a
  second instead of about two.
- Search in large vaults does about half the work per key, and the health
  screen only draws the rows you can see.
- The export wizard no longer drops `j` and `k` from what you type. A file
  password containing them was silently shortened, so the backup was
  encrypted with a different password than the one typed. If you made a
  password-protected export with 1.0.0 and its password has a `j` or a `k`,
  that file opens with the password minus those letters; export again to
  be safe.
- In the editor, `Tab` keeps INSERT mode, so a form can be filled in one go.
- `Space` opens the which-key panel after its 300 ms delay, not up to a
  second later.
- Starting with no account logged in goes to the login screen, and a `bw`
  that is too old or cannot be run gets a screen that says so.

The [changelog](https://github.com/SyscallBrain/lazybw/blob/v1.1.0/CHANGELOG.md)
has the full list.

## Downloads

| File | For |
|---|---|
| `lazybw-1.1.0-x86_64-unknown-linux-musl.tar.gz` | any Linux on x86_64 (static binary) |
| `lazybw-1.1.0-aarch64-unknown-linux-musl.tar.gz` | any Linux on ARM64, including Termux on Android |
| `lazybw_1.1.0-1_amd64.deb`, `lazybw_1.1.0-1_arm64.deb` | Debian, Ubuntu and derivatives |
| `lazybw-1.1.0-1.x86_64.rpm`, `lazybw-1.1.0-1.aarch64.rpm` | Fedora, openSUSE, RHEL and derivatives |
| `lazybw-1.1.0-1-x86_64.pkg.tar.zst`, `lazybw-1.1.0-1-aarch64.pkg.tar.zst` | Arch Linux, Arch Linux ARM |
| `SHA256SUMS` | checksums of all of the above |

On Arch Linux it is also in the AUR, as `lazybw-bin` (this release's binary)
and `lazybw` (built from source).

The container image with `bw` included is on the GitHub Container Registry:

```sh
docker run -it --rm -v lazybw:/home/lazybw ghcr.io/syscallbrain/lazybw:1.1.0
```

lazybw needs the official Bitwarden CLI (`bw`) 2025.9.0 or newer. The
[user guide](https://syscallbrain.github.io/lazybw/) covers installation and
everything else.
